prediction.scope: Two HERCULES.EXE DirectDraw surface lifecycle helpers only: 0x6ff0..0x70c0 (208-byte aligned contribution) and 0x7140..0x7170 (48-byte aligned contribution). No source-TU claim.
prediction.prediction: One ordinary C++ family using the pinned SDK IDirectDrawSurface methods and DDSURFACEDESC should reproduce both helper control flows. At 0x6ff0, the native sequence gates on the state byte and fatal-dialog byte, checks IsLost/Restore on the first surface, then zero-initializes a 0x6c descriptor, sets dwSize, and attempts Lock on the second surface. A nonzero Lock result calls the existing 0x6ec0 setter then 0x6bb0 transition; zero or a null second surface copies descriptor pitch/surface values and sets the state byte. At 0x7140, Unlock is conditional on the same three observed state/pointer predicates and the state byte is then cleared unconditionally. Expect exact full contribution sizes including alignment, equal non-relocation instruction bytes, and a consistent symbol map for direct helper calls and global cells; relocatable object bytes may differ at encoded relocation operands.
prediction.falsifier: Reject this single family if either full COFF contribution size including padding differs from 208/48, any non-relocation byte or control-flow edge differs, the SDK method slot/argument shape disagrees with native calls, the Lock-result branch or descriptor-copy path is inverted, the Unlock gates/state clear differ, or any target global/helper binding is inconsistent. Stop after this measurement; do not run declaration, statement-order, or compiler-flag grids.
